text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar said the Central European Free Trade Agreement (CEFTA) would have to re-consider criteria for accepting new members, as some custom measures within the organisation do not work effectively.

- Trade with CEFTA members accounted for around 36 percent of overall Slovak foreign trade in the first half of this year, with turnover totalling $3.31 billion. Slovakia posted a foreign trade surplus of $208 million with CEFTA countries in the first six months.

- Ivan Gasparovic, Chairman of the Slovak parliament, said after his return from an official visit to Washington that the U.S. congress and senate were unanimous in believing that Slovakia should be accepted to NATO.
SME - Premier Meciar said that government departments would have to reduce their expenditure demands from next year's state budget.
- Meciar said the government and the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) still did not agree on the final shape of the planned EXIM bank.
- NBS Governor Vladimir Masar expects the foreign trade deficit to total 40 to 55 billion crowns at the end of this year.

- The independent doctors union said it insisted on a 3,000 crown wage increase by the end of this year. If the Association of Hospitals does not agree on the pay rise by the end of this month, doctors will strike to support their demands.
- The Opposition Democratic Union (DU) said it would propose the dismissal of culture minister Ivan Hudec and general prosecutor Michal Valo.
- Three foreign tourists, two Czechs and one German, died in the High Tatra Mountains over the weekend.
PRAVDA - Minister of agriculture, Peter Baco, said he did not expect a dramatic increase in food prices. Baco defined a dramatic increase at around 30 percent.
- State subsidies to agriculture will increase by 30 percent, or 2.4 billion crowns, next year. -- Bratislava Newsroom, 42-7-210-3687
